Your first steps to set up a Jupyter project with all the powerful tools and features that the Jupyter Extension has to offer!
Create or open a Jupyter Notebook

contributes.walkthroughs.jupyterWelcome..message:
Right-click in the file explorer and create a new file with an .ipynb extension. Or, open the [Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands) and run the command 
``Create: New Jupyter Notebook``.
[Create New Jupyter Notebook](command:toSide:ipynb.newUntitledIpynb)
 If you have an existing project, you can also [open a folder](command:toSide:workbench.action.files.openFolder) and/or clone a project from GitHub: [clone a Git repository](command:toSide:git.clone).

Click Select Kernel at the top right of the notebook and choose the environment in which to run your kernel. Or, with a notebook opened and in focus, open the [Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands) and run the command: 
``Notebook: Select Notebook Kernel``. 
[Open Command Palette to Select a Jupyter Kernel](command:workbench.action.showCommands)

Selecting or changing a notebook kernel

📅 You can use the [Data Viewer](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/data-science-tutorial#_prepare-the-data) to view, sort, and filter the rows of data. After loading your data, click "Variables" at the top right of the notebook and click the Data Viewer icon to the left of the data table. 
 
[Learn about Data Viewer](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/data-science-tutorial#_prepare-the-data)
 
📒 Debug your notebook using the [Run by Line](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks#_run-by-line) mode to execute a cell one line at a time. Click the Run by Line icon from your cell (play button with lines) or hit F10. 
 
[Learn about Run by Line](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks#_run-by-line)

contributes.walkthroughs.jupyterWelcome..message:
🎨 Explore all the features the Jupyter Extension has to offer by looking for "Jupyter" in the [Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands). 
 📈 Learn more about getting started with data science in [Python](command:workbench.action.openWalkthrough?%7B%22category%22%3A%22ms-python.python%23pythonDataScienceWelcome%22%2C%22step%22%3A%22ms-python.python%23python.createNewNotebook%22%7D) by installing the Python Extension ([search Python extension](command:workbench.extensions.search?"ms-python.python")). 
 📃 Find out more features in our [Tutorials](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks).  
[Learn more](https://aka.ms/AAdar6q)

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.widgetSc: Loads widget (javascript) scripts from a custom CDN, following the provided URL template.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.widgetSc.message:
Defines the location and order of the sources where script files for widgets are downloaded from (e.g., ipywidgets, bqplot, beakerx, ipyleaflet, etc). Not selecting any of these could result in widgets not rendering or functioning correctly. See [here](https://aka.ms/PVSCIPyWidgets) for more information. Once updated, you will need to restart the Kernel. Custom values will be interpreted as URL templates where: 
- `${packageName}` will be replaced with the package name 
- `{fileName}` will be replaced with the file name 
- `${fileNameWithExt}` will be replaced with the file name including `.js` extension 
- `${moduleVersion}` will be replaced with the exact module version 
- `${moduleVersionSpec}` will be replaced with the module version specifier that may include `^` to indicate a range of compatible versions
comment: Do not translate what's inside of the '${..}'. It is an internal syntax for the extension

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.askForLa: Warn the user before trying to open really large data frames.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.askForKe: Warn the user before restarting a kernel.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.exportWi: Enable exporting a Python file into a Jupyter notebook and run all cells when doing so.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.jupyterL: Amount of time (in ms) to wait for the Jupyter Notebook server to start.
Number of times to attempt to connect to the Jupyter Notebook
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.jupyterC: If and when a Jupyter server is started, these arguments will be passed to the Jupyter Notebook CLI. By default, this list is generated by the Jupyter extension.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.notebook:
Set the root directory for Jupyter Notebooks and the Interactive Window running locally.  

**Note:** This does not apply to Remote Jupyter Kernels.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.useDefau: When running Jupyter locally, create a default empty Jupyter config
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.jupyterI: Amount of time (in ms) to wait for an interrupt before asking to restart the Jupyter kernel.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.sendSele: When pressing shift+enter, send selected code in a Python file to the Jupyter interactive window as opposed to the Python terminal.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.normaliz: Selected text will be normalized before it is executed in the Interactive Window.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.splitRun: A file run in the Interactive Window will be run in individual cells if it has them.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.sendSele: This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.textEditor.executeSelection.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.variable: Types to exclude from showing in the Interactive variable explorer
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.codeRegu: Regular expression used to identify code cells. All code until the next match is considered part of this cell.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.cellMarker.codeRegex.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.defaultC: Cell marker used for delineating a cell in a Python file.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.cellMarker.default
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.markdown: Regular expression used to identify markdown cells. All comments after this expression are considered part of the markdown.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.cellMarker.markdownRegex.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.themeMat: In the Interactive window and Notebook Editor theme matplotlib outputs to match the VS Code editor theme.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.decorate: Draw a highlight behind the currently active cell, or all cells, in a Python file.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.cellMarker.decorateCells.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.enableCe: Enables code lens for 'cells' in a Python file.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.codeLens.enable.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.enableAu: Enables moving to the next cell when clicking on a 'Run Cell' code lens.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.textEditor.autoMoveToNextCell.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.allowUna: Allow for connecting the Interactive window to a https Jupyter server that does not have valid certificates. This can be a security risk, so only use it for known and trusted servers.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.codeLens: Set of commands to put as code lens above a cell.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.codeLens.commands.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.debugCod: Set of debug commands to put as code lens above a cell while debugging.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.codeLens.debugCommands.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.debugpyD: Path to debugpy bits for debugging cells.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.stopOnFi: When debugging a cell, stop on the first line.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.disableJ: When true, disables Jupyter from being automatically started for you. You must instead run a cell to start deepnote.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.addGotoC.message: After running a cell, add a 'Goto' code lens on the cell. Note, disabling all code lenses disables this code lens as well.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.addGotoC: This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.codeLens.enableGotoCell.
List of Python environments to be excluded from the kernel picker.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.interact.message: Behavior of the Interactive Window. 'perFile' will create a new interactive window for every file that runs a cell. 'single' allows a single window. 'multiple' allows the creation of multiple.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.interact: Experimental. The interactive window will use a notebook as the editor model.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.creationMode.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.pythonCe: Enable folding regions for code cells in Python files. This setting requires a reload of VS Code.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.textEditor.cellFolding.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.interact.message: Where to open an Interactive Window that is not associated with a Python file. 'beside' will open the interactive window to the right of the active editor. 'active' will open the interactive window in place of the active editor. 'secondGroup' will open the interactive window in the second editor group.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.interact: This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.viewColumn.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.magicCom: Uncomment shell assignments (#!), line magic (#!%) and cell magic (#!%%) when parsing code cells.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.textEditor.magicCommandsAsComments.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.pythonEx.message: The method to use when exporting a notebook to a Python file. 'direct' will copy over the code directly as is. 'commentMagics' will comment out lines starting with line magics (%), cell magics (%%), and shell commands(!). 'nbconvert' will install nbconvert and use that for the conversion which can translate iPython syntax into Python syntax.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.runStart.message:
A series of Python instructions or iPython magic commands. Can be either an array of strings or a single string with commands separated by '\n'. Commands will be silently executed whenever a Jupyter kernel is started or restarted. For instance, set this to '%load_ext autoreload
%autoreload 2' to automatically reload changes made to imported files without having to restart the Jupyter kernel.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.debugJus: When debugging, only step through user-written code. Disable this to allow stepping into library code.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.showOutl: Show the Outline button in the Jupyter notebook toolbar.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.newCellO: Append a new empty cell to an interactive window file on running the currently last cell.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.interactiveWindow.textEditor.autoAddNewCell.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.pythonCo: Characters which trigger auto completion on a Python Jupyter kernel.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.completionTriggerCharacters.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.completi:
Mapping of characters which trigger auto completion in a Jupyter kernel language. Following is an example of trigger characters for rust and julia kernel languages:
```json 
{
  "julia": ["."],
  "rust": [".",":"] 
}
```
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.logKerne: Creates separate output panels for kernels/Jupyter server console output

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.excludeU.message: Add PYTHONNOUSERSITE to kernels before starting. This prevents global/user site-packages from being used in the PYTHONPATH of the kernel.

deepnote.configuration.deepnote.enableEx: Enables Jedi support for extended IntelliSense completions in running Python Jupyter kernels for Python (see this [setting](https://ipython.readthedocs.io/en/stable/config/options/terminal.html?highlight=use_jedi#configtrait-Completer.use_jedi)). This can greatly impact notebook cell execution performance. Use with caution.
This setting has been deprecated in favor of deepnote.enableExtendedPythonKernelCompletions.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.enableKe: Enable code completions in Notebooks and Interactive Windows using results from the associated Jupyter kernel.
deepnote.configuration.deepnote.formatSt: Inject stack frame links into the stored traceback for the notebook.
This setting has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
